# relgap completion

Generate the autocompletion script for relgap for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

## Usage

```sh
relgap completion <shell>
```

## Shells

| Shell | Command |
|---|---|
| [bash](#bash) | `relgap completion bash` |
| [clink](#clink) | `relgap completion clink` |
| [elvish](#elvish) | `relgap completion elvish` |
| [fish](#fish) | `relgap completion fish` |
| [nushell](#nushell) | `relgap completion nushell` |
| [oil](#oil) | `relgap completion oil` |
| [powershell](#powershell) | `relgap completion powershell` |
| [tcsh](#tcsh) | `relgap completion tcsh` |
| [xonsh](#xonsh) | `relgap completion xonsh` |
| [zsh](#zsh) | `relgap completion zsh` |

The [global flags](/cli/global-flags) work with every command. The shell commands ignore `--format`.

### bash

Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(relgap completion bash)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

**Linux**

```text
relgap completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/relgap
```

**macOS**

```text
relgap completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/relgap
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

### clink

Generate the autocompletion script for clink. carapace, built into relgap, writes it.

Save the script as a Lua file in a clink scripts directory, such as
%LOCALAPPDATA%\clink\relgap.lua:

```text
relgap completion clink > %LOCALAPPDATA%\clink\relgap.lua
```

### elvish

Generate the autocompletion script for elvish. carapace, built into relgap, writes it.

Add this line to ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv:

```text
eval (relgap completion elvish | slurp)
```

### fish

Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
relgap completion fish | source
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

```text
relgap completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/relgap.fish
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

### nushell

Generate the autocompletion script for nushell. carapace, built into relgap, writes it.

The script defines $relgap\_completer. Save it, source it from config.nu and use it as
the external completer (or call it from yours when the first span is relgap):

```text
relgap completion nushell | save --force ~/.config/nushell/relgap.nu

# config.nu
source ~/.config/nushell/relgap.nu
$env.config.completions.external = {enable: true, completer: $relgap_completer}
```

### oil

Generate the autocompletion script for oil. carapace, built into relgap, writes it.

Add this line to your oils startup file (~/.config/oils/oshrc or yshrc):

```text
source <(relgap completion oil)
```

### powershell

Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
relgap completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
to your powershell profile.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

### tcsh

Generate the autocompletion script for tcsh. carapace, built into relgap, writes it.

Add this line to ~/.tcshrc:

```text
eval `relgap completion tcsh`
```

### xonsh

Generate the autocompletion script for xonsh. carapace, built into relgap, writes it.

Add this line to ~/.xonshrc:

```text
exec($(relgap completion xonsh))
```

### zsh

Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need
to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

```text
echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc
```

To load completions in your current shell session:

```text
source <(relgap completion zsh)
```

To load completions for every new session, execute once:

**Linux**

```text
relgap completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_relgap"
```

**macOS**

```text
relgap completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_relgap
```

You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

| Flag | Description | Type | Default | Values | Config key | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--no-descriptions` | disable completion descriptions | bool |  |  |  |  |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command finished. With --fail-on, nothing matched. |
| 1 | The command failed: a read, a write, a child process or a check failed. |
| 2 | Wrong usage: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or argument, an invalid config file, or a prompt with no terminal. |
| 130 | Interrupted by Ctrl-C (SIGINT) or a cancelled context. |

All codes are listed on the [exit codes](/reference/exit-codes) page.

## Examples

```sh
relgap completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/relgap
relgap completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_relgap"
relgap completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/relgap.fish
```
